 Building Durable Real Estate Portfolios at Morgan Stanley – Lauren Hochfelder (EP.514) Jul 30, 2026

 
 
 
 
 
 Lauren Hochfelder is Head of Global Real Assets at
Morgan Stanley, where she oversees a team of 300 investment
professionals across 13 countries, managing $80
billion across real estate,
infrastructure, equity and credit. Lauren joined Morgan
Stanley as an investment banking analyst directly out of Yale 26
years ago and has spent her entire career at the firm, helping
build one of the industry's leading platforms.

 
   
 
 Our conversation traces Lauren's journey from analyst
to Global Head and the evolution of Morgan Stanley's real estate
business before, during, and after the Global Financial Crisis. We
cover the firm’s thematic approach to investing behind structural
demand tailwinds, combination of global perspectives and
on-the-ground teams, operational improvements to assets, portfolio
construction, and themes across industrial real estate and
infrastructure, senior housing, and net lease properties. We also
touch on riskier areas of real estate and Lauren’s new role adding
infrastructure to her real estate oversight.

 About the Podcast 
 
 
 Allocator and asset management expert, Ted Seides, conducts in-depth interviews with leaders in the institutional investing industry. Guests include Chief Investment Officers from leading allocators, asset managers, strategists, thought leaders, and many more. Our mission is to learn, share, and help implement the process of premier investors. Learn more and join our community at capitalallocators.com.
